concept.name: Stochastic oscillator
concept.definition: George Lane's momentum indicator (late 1950s) measuring where the close sits within the high-low range of the look-back period, bounded 0-100 and published in Fast, Slow, and Full versions. Lane's premise: momentum changes direction before price.
concept.intuition: In an uptrend prices tend to close near the top of their recent range; the stochastic quantifies that tendency.
concept.mechanics: %K = (C - LL)/(HH - LL)*100 over (default) 14 periods; %D = 3-period SMA of %K acts as the signal line; the Slow version smooths %K once more. Readings above 80 are overbought, below 20 oversold; signals come from %K/%D crosses, divergences, and Lane's bull/bear set-ups.
concept.formula: %K = 100 * (C - LL_n)/(HH_n - LL_n); %D = SMA_3(%K); HH_n and LL_n are the highest high and lowest low over n periods.
concept.failure_modes: Can remain overbought or oversold through an entire strong trend, so counter-trend signals fail repeatedly; fast versions whipsaw, and signals work best in trading ranges or zigzag trends.
concept.misconceptions: The stochastic does not follow price or volume — per Lane it follows the speed (momentum) of price; and an overbought reading alone is not a sell signal.
concept.example: With a 14-day high of 110, low of 100, and close of 108, %K = (108-100)/(110-100)*100 = 80.
